chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who doubts during the obligatory tawaf. He said: He repeats it whenever he doubts. I said: May I be your ransom, what if he doubts in the supererogatory tawaf? He said: He builds upon the lesser number.

So it does not contradict the first report, because this report is to be understood as referring to one who doubted before completing seven, since one in that state has no way to ascertain seven circuits with certainty. The first report refers to one who has completed seven circuits and is certain of them, and only doubted about what was in excess of them, so he does not pay attention to that doubt. And that which clarifies what we have mentioned is...

key_terms.سَبْعَةَ أَشْوَاطٍ: the seven circuits that constitute a complete tawaf
key_terms.طَوَافِ الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory tawaf that must be validly completed
key_terms.عَلَى الْيَقِينِ: with certainty, free of unresolved doubt
key_terms.يَبْنِي عَلَى الْأَقَلِّ: he proceeds on the basis of the lesser number he is certain of
key_terms.يُعِيدُ: he repeats the act from the beginning

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone doubts the number of circuits during obligatory or supererogatory tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of doubt during tawaf, distinguishing between obligatory and supererogatory tawaf. In obligatory tawaf, doubt requires repetition, while in supererogatory tawaf one proceeds on the basis of the lesser number. The appended explanation reconciles this report with another by distinguishing doubt before completing seven circuits from doubt after seven have been certainly completed.
